arguments.head: codex/git-push-pull-integration
arguments.title: Separate Sun push and pull and integrate with Git commands
arguments.body:
Sun push currently joins remote history while publishing, so users cannot inspect that join locally before it reaches the remote. This change makes `sun push` publish recorded Sun history without moving the local branch and reject non-fast-forward updates. New `sun pull [remote] [branch]` fetches and joins history locally while preserving the recorded local snapshot and working files.

Optional shell integration (`eval "$(sun shell-init)"`) automatically initializes Sun on the first Git push or pull. Successful Git pushes invoke Sun publication, including up-to-date Git branches; successful Git pulls invoke the same Sun pull implementation for the branch actually pulled. Fetch only downloads history. Git handles file merges, and Git's rebase/fast-forward flags do not change Sun's history-join behavior. Sun failures warn without overriding Git's exit status; raw transcript sharing remains off during automatic setup.

Validation: 206 tests passed with `python3 -m unittest discover -v`, plus the subsequently added explicit fetch-versus-pull source-branch test passed separately. Coverage includes divergence rejection, pull-then-push, unchanged Git commits, dirty files and index preservation, dry runs, failed pulls, rebases, renamed push destinations, separate push URLs, and collaborator operation/check preservation.
